outline.chapter_title: Why Parameter-Efficient Finetuning? Motivation and Overview
outline.description: Introduce the need to adapt large foundation models without retraining, situate BOFT within the landscape of parameter-efficient finetuning, and summarize the paper’s goals and contributions.
subtopics: The rise of foundation models and the cost of full finetuning
Three PEFT families: model finetuning, adapters, and prompts
Why model finetuning (no inference latency) remains attractive
From LoRA to OFT: preserving knowledge during adaptation
Paper overview: information transmission view, butterfly parameterization, BOFT method
Key contributions and claimed benefits across vision, language, and diffusion

outline.description: Provide foundational linear algebra and optimization concepts needed to understand OFT and BOFT.
subtopics: Orthogonal matrices: definitions, properties, and the Stiefel/orthogonal groups
Skew-symmetric matrices and Cayley transform
Spectral norm and singular value decomposition (SVD)
Angles between vectors (neurons) and why orthogonality preserves them
Sparse vs low-rank structures: parameter-efficiency perspectives
Block structures, permutations, and dense vs sparse connectivity

outline.chapter_title: Background on PEFT: LoRA, OFT, and Beyond
outline.description: Survey parameter-efficient finetuning methods and position OFT and BOFT among them.
subtopics: LoRA: additive low-rank reparameterization and its popularity
Dynamic rank variants and budget allocation across layers
Adapter tuning and prompt/prefix tuning in brief
OFT: multiplicative orthogonal reparameterization and angle preservation
Comparative strengths and weaknesses: expressivity, stability, parameters
When orthogonality helps: preserving spectral properties and stability

outline.description: Explain OFT’s formulation, training, and known limitations that motivate BOFT.
subtopics: OFT forward pass: W^finetuned = R W^0 with R orthogonal
Cayley parameterization for enforcing orthogonality during training
Zero/identity initialization and training dynamics
Block-diagonal OFT: parameter savings and inductive bias
Limitations: fixed sparsity pattern, reduced expressiveness, inability to recover classic transforms
Open question: Can we get dense R with fewer parameters than O(d^2)?

outline.chapter_title: An Information Transmission View of Orthogonal Factorization
outline.description: Reframe composing dense orthogonal matrices from sparse factors as an information transmission problem on a layered graph.
subtopics: Matrix multiplication as layered connectivity: grid graph with d × (m+1) nodes
Edges represent nonzeros; paths represent information flow
Desiderata for parameter efficiency: dense connectivity and minimum free edges
Orthogonality constraints: full-rank layers and coupling of edges
Comparing direct dense R (O(d^2)) vs factorizations with fewer edges
Illustrative examples: when factorization fails to be dense vs succeeds

outline.chapter_title: Butterfly Structures and the FFT: A Primer
outline.description: Introduce butterfly networks from Cooley–Tukey FFT and why they are efficient for global information exchange.
subtopics: Cooley–Tukey FFT and recursive divide-and-conquer
Butterfly graphs: topology and communication properties
Butterfly matrices as products of sparse blocks
O(d log d) connectivity vs O(d^2) dense connectivity
Connections to fast linear transforms (DFT, DCT, Hadamard)
Intuition for why butterfly sparsity still enables global mixing

outline.description: Define butterfly factors and components, show how to ensure orthogonality, and present the BOFT parameterization.
subtopics: Butterfly factor B^F(k) and block structure with diag vectors
Recursive butterfly matrix B(d) via components 𝜏B(d,k)
Block butterfly variant: replacing scalars by b×b blocks
Ensuring orthogonality: Cayley on 2×2 or 2b×2b blocks; permutations preserve nonzero patterns
BOFT(m, b): product of m orthogonal butterfly components
Special cases: BOFT(1, b) = block-diagonal OFT; BOFT(1, d) = full OFT
Parameter counts: BOFT with O((b−1) d m / 2) parameters; O(d log d) when b=2 and m=log d
Dense R from BOFT with m = log(2d/b): contrast with OFT’s need for b=d

outline.chapter_title: Training BOFT: Initialization, Regularization, and Inference
outline.description: Explain practical training mechanisms unique to BOFT and their rationale.
subtopics: Identity initialization of butterfly components via zero skew-symmetric parameters
Multiplicative Dropout: randomly identity-replacing blocks/components
Why conventional additive dropout doesn’t directly apply
Training overhead vs inference cost: multiply-in at the end for zero latency
Numerical stability: preserving spectral norm and gradient behavior
Implementation notes for GPUs/TPUs and efficient permutations

outline.chapter_title: Expressivity, Theory, and Properties of BOFT
outline.description: Analyze the expressive power of BOFT and its mathematical properties compared to OFT and LoRA.
subtopics: Approximation of random orthogonal matrices: empirical trends with (m, b)
Expressivity theorem: BOFT more expressive than OFT with same block size
Kaleidoscope hierarchy: alternating butterfly and transposed butterfly products to cover full O(d)
Trade-off: expressivity vs regularity and generalization implications
Spectral property preservation: spectral norm unchanged by left-orthogonal multiplication
Bilinear similarity perspective: learning R in w_i^0^T R x with orthogonality constraints
Inductive bias from structured sparsity and fast transform priors

outline.chapter_title: Design Choices: How to Set m, b, and Placement
outline.description: Provide practical guidance for configuring BOFT under parameter budgets and task constraints.

Budgeting: balancing O(d log d) vs O(b d m) parameter regimes
Where to apply BOFT: attention projections, MLPs, embeddings, normalization choices
Layer-wise allocation and sharing strategies
Dropout rates (component-level and block-level) and regularization
Initialization and learning rate schedules; optimizers and weight decay
Handling non-power-of-two dimensions (padding, partial butterflies, permutations)
